destination.title: Microphysical dissipation and potential control
destination.question: Which interactions generate sufficient dissipation and fluctuations while preserving the conditions needed for inflation?
destination.summary: Connects microscopic interaction structures, thermal consistency and naturalness without identifying their protection mechanisms.

systems: Interacting scalar, fermionic, mediator and gauge sectors
targets: Dissipative approaches to the eta problem
regimes: Frequency-dependent response, including nearly cold initial conditions
assumptions: A phenomenological friction term alone does not establish microscopic consistency
Protection by symmetry and tolerance of a large inflaton mass are distinct routes
conventions: Interaction hierarchies and coefficient laws are not interchangeable
includes: Scalar relaxation as a methodological neighbor
excludes: Universal validity of a low-frequency thermal coefficient
A general proof that strong dissipation preserves every potential

sources.title: Warm Inflation and its Microphysical Basis

evidence.text: How can interacting quantum fields generate dissipation, radiation and stochastic inflaton fluctuations during inflation, and under what conditions do these effects support viable warm inflation?

sources.title: Warm Little Inflaton

evidence.text: Can warm inflation with T>H be sustained by direct couplings to only a few light fields while protecting the inflaton potential against dangerous radiative and thermal mass corrections?

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Which microscopic interaction regimes can supply dissipation strong enough to affect inflation without invalidating the potential through thermal corrections? The three laws represent different mediator hierarchies and protection mechanisms.

sources.title: Warm Inflation in the light of Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can the interactions required for dissipation leave the inflaton potential sufficiently stable? Direct Yukawa couplings create a tradeoff: larger coupling helps energy transfer but increases induced fermion masses and thermal corrections to the inflaton.

sources.title: Warm inflation within a supersymmetric distributed mass model

evidence.text: How do inflaton-dependent tower masses and thermal mass corrections enter dissipation and thermal corrections to an inflationary potential?

sources.title: Minimal warm inflation with complete medium response

evidence.text: How can warm-inflation evolution incorporate medium response across all relevant frequency scales, including an initially almost cold bath, rather than applying the low-frequency thermal friction coefficient throughout?

sources.title: The Warm Inflation Story

evidence.text: Can interactions sustain particle production, dissipation and primordial fluctuations during inflation, with microphysics fast enough to survive expansion? The review also asks whether this dynamics improves first-principles inflation model building.

sources.title: Strong dissipative behavior in quantum field theory

evidence.text: Under what microscopic conditions can an initially displaced scalar order parameter, whose fundamental dynamics is second order in time, acquire strongly dissipative, effectively first-order Ginzburg–Landau relaxation through quadratic interactions with other scalar fields?

sources.title: Is warm inflation possible?

evidence.text: Can thermal dissipation sustain a self-consistent, prolonged inflationary phase when thermalization, adiabaticity, thermal masses, and radiation production are imposed simultaneously?

sources.title: Warm Inflation and its Microphysical Basis

evidence.text: A slow-background derivative expansion localizes the response and gives Υ=(i/2)∂ωΣρ(0,ω)|ω=0. Spectral-function calculations determine coefficients; a quasiparticle Boltzmann treatment separately connects particle-production sources to the radiation energy equation.

sources.title: Warm Little Inflaton

evidence.text: Estimate dissipation from high-temperature on-shell fermion contributions, using their finite-temperature decay widths and thermal masses. The approximate numerical coefficient is obtained by evaluating the width near the momentum p≈3.24T that dominates the integral.

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Differentiate the dissipation law at fixed coefficient and exponent, replace temperature perturbations through the bath equation of state, then solve the coupled fluctuation problem. The response function requires that additional dynamics; the algebraic variation only exposes the coupling.

sources.title: Warm Inflation in the light of Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Translate the bounds to common conventions, intersect them jointly, and distinguish algebraic feasibility from realization by a physical trajectory. In this paper, the operation adds the omitted comparison between the slope-implied tensor floor and the excursion-implied tensor cap.

sources.title: Warm inflation within a supersymmetric distributed mass model

evidence.text: Weight the momentum-dependent on-shell rate by a Bose-Einstein distribution and normalize by number density. Factor out mass and coupling terms before approximating the remaining inverse-energy integral.

sources.title: Minimal warm inflation with complete medium response

evidence.text: Derives a nonlocal scalar equation from first-order density-matrix linear response. One-sided Fourier/Laplace transforms and contour deformation identify late-time dynamics through nearby singularities. A fourth-derivative counterterm is introduced to cancel the correlator's ultraviolet divergence.

sources.title: Warm inflation model building

evidence.text: How does microphysically motivated dissipation change inflationary dynamics, primordial spectra and supersymmetric model building for monomial, hybrid and hilltop potentials? This invited review also extends earlier model analyses.

sources.title: Warm inflation solution to the eta problem

evidence.text: Can dissipation during inflation satisfy slow-roll and density-perturbation requirements with mφ≫H, η≫1 and sub-Planckian inflaton amplitudes, thereby avoiding the usual eta problem without symmetry protection of an exceptionally flat potential?

sources.title: Recent Developments in Warm Inflation

evidence.text: How does dissipative particle production realize warm inflation, support viable microscopic models, modify primordial perturbations, and permit compatibility with observations and swampland conjectures?

sources.title: Towards a reliable effective field theory of inflation

evidence.text: Can a perturbative QFT model with renormalizable matter interactions sustain observationally viable inflation through strong dissipation, with a super-Hubble inflaton mass and sub-Planckian excursion, thereby addressing the usual inflaton naturalness problem?

sources.title: Swampland, axions, and minimal warm inflation

evidence.text: How do expansion, inflaton motion, and a thermal gauge bath exchange energy during inflation?

sources.title: The early universe is ACT-ing warm

evidence.text: Can symmetry-protected warm little inflaton models with simple monomial potentials accommodate the paper's ACT-era scalar tilt and tensor bounds, including strong dissipation, when both fermionic and scalar dissipative channels are treated numerically?

sources.title: Warm pseudoscalar inflation

evidence.text: Can a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled directly to light SU(2) gauge fields sustain warm inflation while avoiding dangerous thermal corrections, and produce acceptable scalar/tensor perturbations and small non-Gaussianity in a dissipative regime with f<Mp?

sources.title: Dynamical Inflaton Coupled to Strongly Interacting Matter

evidence.text: Can a dynamical inflaton and expanding spacetime be coupled self-consistently to strongly interacting matter, producing inflation, reheating and eventual thermal QFT domination?

sources.title: Axion monodromy inflation, trapping mechanisms and the swampland

evidence.text: Can energy transfer into particles sustain inflation on a steep axion potential over a Planckian or smaller excursion? The paper compares self-production of the inflaton with repeated production of additional fields and asks whether either mechanism permits an exit.

sources.title: Warm quintessential inflation

evidence.text: Can a single surviving scalar account for inflation and present dark energy while dissipation supplies reheating, avoiding inflaton decay in quintessential inflation?

sources.title: Reheating After Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a thermal effective theory describing oscillatory reheating satisfy the conjectured restrictions on scalar potentials and field excursions? The paper compares this issue with warm inflation, in which interactions generate radiation during the inflationary stage.

sources.title: Does fractal universe favour warm inflation: Observational support?

evidence.text: Can a prescribed fractal spacetime measure support warm inflation in weak and strong dissipation, and can selected measure profiles and dissipation laws yield predictions inside the historical Planck 2018 scalar-index/tensor-ratio contours?
